title: Confirmed bug
text: elastix's center of rotation is lost. MatrixRetrieval only reads TransformParameters and never CenterOfRotationPoint . An elastix EulerTransform is worth R·(x − c) + t + c ; the reconstructed sitk.Euler3DTransform has its center at the origin and is worth R·x + t . The two only coincide if c is the origin or if R = I . Since AutomaticTransformInitialization is active and the center of rotation is derived from the fixed image (T1, which is only centered in Orientation mode), the gap (I − R)·c is generally non-zero.

title: A hypothesis to test rather than to believe: if the module still gives correct results in practice, it is like…
text: A hypothesis to test rather than to believe: if the module still gives correct results in practice, it is likely because the volumes already arrive close to the origin — PRE_ASO recenters T2 and ASO orients T1 — so that c ≈ 0 and (I − R)·c stays small. That makes the result dependent on a prior centering that is guaranteed nowhere. Measure the gap on a real case before drawing conclusions.

title: Trap

title: The function does not do what its name says
text: It is called run_icp_point_to_plane ; it does compute fixed_normals via compute_normals(inplace=True) on a copy of the fixed mesh — and never uses them . The criterion minimized is ‖R·s + t − d‖² , i.e. classic point-to-point . The normals are computed then discarded on every call, twice per patient, on a marching-cubes isosurface that can run to hundreds of thousands of faces.

title: Code / paper divergence
text: The code diverges from the paper at the last step. The abstract describes an unsupervised approach — dimensionality reduction (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP) then Spectral Clustering , with UMAP+RBF giving the best silhouette score. The module, on the other hand, ships three supervised binary LightGBM classifiers trained on 14 fixed features. The two are not the same model; nothing in the repository links the LightGBMs' training labels to the paper's clusters, and the training script is not versioned.

title: Two engines, one window
text: The module picks the right engine on its own based on your data: CBCT for a volume, IOS for an intraoral scan. All you do is say what type your files are and which points you want.

title: "Nothing comes out, or the points look wrong"
text: First check that the models were actually downloaded, then that the data type you checked matches your files. A CBCT processed as an intraoral scan won't produce anything usable.

title: Intraoral scans: teeth need to be identified first
text: On an intraoral scan, the engine aims its measurements tooth by tooth. If your file doesn't have crown identification yet, ALI runs it automatically along the way — expect extra time on the first attempt.

title: DICOM import
text: Use .nii.gz files instead. The module's DICOM path doesn't work in automatic mode.

title: Disk space
text: The temporary folder isn't cleared afterward. On long series, remember to clean it out from time to time.

page: AMASSS — segmenting structures from a CBCT
title: "Small FOV" changes nothing about the computation
text: The checkbox that switches to a "high definition" list (teeth, root canal, and mandibular canal included) only changes which checkboxes are shown on screen. It does not reduce the field of view or the resolution of the computation — don't expect it to run faster or produce a finer result.

page: AMASSS — segmenting structures from a CBCT
title: Root canal is checked by default, with no model
text: "Root canal" is checked by default in the structure list, but the published model bundle has no model for it. Checking it produces neither an error nor a segmentation: the failure is silent, the structure is simply missing from the result.

page: AMASSS — segmenting structures from a CBCT
title: DICOM import
text: The interface offers "DICOM Files" as an input type, but no DICOM conversion actually happens before the computation runs: a DICOM input produces nothing. Use .nii.gz or .nrrd files instead.

page: AMASSS — segmenting structures from a CBCT
title: Don't run two modules at once
text: AMASSS unconditionally wipes its temporary working folder every time it starts. That same folder is shared with AREG_CBCT and VFACE, which call AMASSS behind the scenes. If you run two of these modules at the same time on the same machine, one can wipe the other's working folder mid-run — let one computation finish before starting another.

page: AREG_CBCT — register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: Which one to pick
text: Already have masks? Semi-Automated. No masks, but T1 scans already oriented the same way? Fully-Automated. Neither? Orientation & Registration. In all three modes, you check one or more reference regions ( Cranial Base , Mandible , Maxilla ): each one runs its own independent registration, with its own output.

page: AREG_CBCT — register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: A patient goes missing, with no error message
text: T1/T2 pairing only works with the _T1 and _T2 suffixes in the file name. Any other convention ( _T3 , _baseline , a date…) keeps AREG_CBCT from recognizing the pair, and that patient is silently dropped — nothing is shown to flag it. If a patient is missing from the output, the first thing to check is that patient's file names.

page: AREG_CBCT — register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: Avoid mask keywords in a scan's file name
text: AREG_CBCT recognizes a mask file by keywords in its name ( seg , mask , pred , or the region's abbreviation — cb , mand , max ). The first file that matches is used as-is, with no check that it's actually a mask. A scan named, say, P1_T1_MAX.nii.gz could therefore be mistaken for a maxilla mask.

page: AREG_CBCT — register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: DICOM import
text: Convert your CBCT scans to .nii.gz before running AREG_CBCT. DICOM input is only offered in Orientation & Registration mode, and stays fragile even there: starting from already-converted files avoids the surprise.

page: AREG_CBCT — register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: The saved matrix can drift slightly from the best alignment found
text: The .tfm file and the registered CBCT stay consistent with each other, but both can drift a bit from the alignment the registration actually found as optimal. The gap depends on where the skull sits in the volume, and stays small when your images are already well centered — which is the case after a run through Orientation & Registration. If you reuse this matrix elsewhere, in AutoMatrix for instance, always check the overlay by eye before trusting it.

page: AREG_CBCT — register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: "Include Approximation Step" no longer does anything
text: The checkbox stays checked by default in the interface, but it has no effect on the result: don't count on it to speed up or refine a registration that's giving you trouble.

page: AREG_IOS — register two scans of the same patient
title: Two modes, one per arch
text: Butterfly (upper arch): the module predicts the stable palatal patch itself, with a network, and uses it as the registration anchor. MGL (lower arch): there's no palate down there, so the module builds a band along the mucogingival line instead, from landmarks it places automatically.

page: AREG_IOS — register two scans of the same patient
title: No compatible graphics card
text: In Butterfly mode, the palatal patch inference requires a CUDA GPU, full stop. On a machine without a compatible GPU, this mode fails outright. Use MGL on those machines, or process the upper arch elsewhere.

page: AREG_IOS — register two scans of the same patient
title: File naming: order matters
text: Put the arch marker before the timepoint marker in the filename ( P001_Upper_T1.vtk ), not after ( P001_T1_Upper.vtk ): in the wrong order, one of the output matrices won't be found — with no blocking error, the run finishes but an expected file is simply missing. Also avoid the same words (Upper, Lower, U, L, Mx, Md…) in parent folder names: they're read from the full path and can throw off the upper/lower sorting for the whole batch.

page: AREG_IOS — register two scans of the same patient
title: A failed orientation silently breaks the patch
text: If the canonical orientation step can't be computed — for instance because the reference teeth weren't identified — processing doesn't stop: the network still runs, on a badly oriented scan, and nothing flags it. Always check the resulting patch visually before trusting it.

page: AREG_IOS — register two scans of the same patient
title: MGL never produces a transform
text: Whichever regime you pick, auto or semi-auto, MGL mode writes no .tfm file at all. You get the registered surfaces, but not the transform that produced them.

page: AREG_IOS — register two scans of the same patient
title: Output folder and file formats
text: The output folder must already exist: AREG_IOS doesn't create missing subfolders. And your files keep their original extension on write even though the content is always rewritten in VTK format — a .stl or .obj coming out is not a strictly valid STL or OBJ file, so keep it for Slicer rather than handing it to another program.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT — place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: Three ways to get there
text: Depending on what you already have — nothing, raw scans, or landmarks already placed — the module offers three modes that don't ask for the same input files. See "Three modes" below before you start.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT — place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: No matrix is written
text: Registration produces surfaces that are already transformed, not a matrix file. Unlike AREG_IOS or AREG_CBCT, you cannot reopen the result and nudge it with the mouse: if the alignment is off, the fix is to rerun — with different landmarks or a different setting — not to correct it by hand.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT — place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: One scanned arch means the patient is dropped
text: Every patient must provide both arches, scan and landmarks included. If even one is missing — say, only one arch was ever scanned — the patient disappears from the result with no visible error, only a line in the log.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT — place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: Only T0, T1 and T2 are recognized
text: The clinical timepoint is read from the file name, and only those three values count. A file marked T3 or beyond matches nothing: the patient is simply left out.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT — place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: The CBCT surface threshold is fixed
text: The surface extracted from the CBCT for registration always uses the same threshold value, whatever your scanner or reconstruction. On a CBCT whose units aren't calibrated, the resulting surface may not correspond to bone or teeth at all, and the registration then runs against noise.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT — place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: The progress bar can announce more patients than it will deliver
text: The interface's counter also recognizes .nrrd , .nii and .gipl for the CBCT. The engine itself only accepts .nii.gz : a patient counted at the start may never actually be processed.

title: Two data types, two ways of working
text: You first tell ASO what kind of files you have: CBCT for a volume, IOS for an intraoral scan. For each, two modes are available. Fully-Automated asks only for your raw scans: ASO places the landmarks it needs itself (via a network, for a CBCT) or segments the teeth (for a scan) before orienting. Semi-Automated skips that prediction step and works directly on landmarks or teeth you have already identified — faster, but it assumes that preparatory work already exists.

title: CBCT semi-automatic: don't run it on its own
text: On a CBCT, the semi-automatic mode needs a transform file that only the automatic mode produces , as part of its recentring step. If you run the semi mode directly on scans that ASO has never processed, it fails patient after patient. In practice, for CBCT, semi-automatic only makes sense as a second pass — for instance to redo the orientation of a series that has already gone through the automatic mode once.

title: Your CBCT landmark files are gone
text: In semi-automatic mode, ASO starts by merging every landmark file it finds in your input folder into a single file — then deletes the originals . Keep a copy of your .mrk.json files elsewhere before running a job, especially if the input folder is also where you keep your only copy of those landmarks.

title: Occlusion: name your files Upper / Lower unambiguously
text: Occlusion mode pairs the upper and lower arches by file name ( Upper / _U_ or Lower / _L_ ). A file whose name carries none of these markers is silently treated as a lower arch — with no error message. Check your file names before turning this option on.

title: Rerunning on a folder that already has output does nothing
text: If an output file already exists under the expected name, ASO does not rewrite it and still reports success. After fixing a setting, point to an empty output folder rather than rerunning on the same one.

page: Agent — let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Read this before you try it
text: As the repository stands today, Agent cannot locate the tools it wants to launch . Unless you configure it manually, any attempt to run a tool fails. The mode that only answers, without executing anything, is not affected and works normally.

page: Agent — let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Nothing to install by hand on the Slicer side
text: The required Python packages install themselves automatically on first launch, inside Slicer's own Python.

page: Agent — let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Read every line, carefully
text: For most tools, the mapping between what Agent believes it's passing and what the tool actually expects is off. A run can therefore start with wrong values without any error warning you beforehand — the confirmation dialog is your only real check.

page: Agent — let a local assistant pick the tool
title: "Nothing launches, or the error makes no sense"
text: As the repository stands, Agent can't find the scripts it wants to run on its own: unless you tell it yourself where they are, execution fails before it even starts. The automatic repair step that follows can't fix this — the problem isn't in the parameters, it's in the script's path.

page: Agent — let a local assistant pick the tool
title: A run starting with wrong values
text: See above: always check the confirmation dialog before approving. A parameter mismatch usually shows up only by eye, in that dialog — not in an error message.

page: Agent — let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Everything is slow without a graphics card
text: If the model server is running without a GPU, expect each reply to take roughly a minute and a half . A back-and-forth conversation adds up to minutes, not seconds.

page: AutoCrop3D — crop a series of volumes
title: The ROI must be an axis-aligned box, saved as-is
text: The fast crop path completely ignores the orientation and coordinate system declared in the ROI file: it only reads the center and size, and assumes a box aligned with the volume's axes. A rotated ROI gets treated as if it weren't, and an ROI saved in the wrong coordinate system shifts the center with no error message at all. The fast path only works with straight boxes, saved the way Slicer stores them by default; for a genuinely rotated ROI, see below.

page: AutoCrop3D — crop a series of volumes
title: A folder with exactly one ROI file → error
text: If you're using per-patient ROIs but the folder holds only a single .mrk.json file, the module errors out instead of applying it to every volume. In that case, point it directly at that file as a single shared ROI rather than at the folder containing it.

page: AutoCrop3D — crop a series of volumes
title: Per-patient ROI: matching breaks on an underscore
text: Volume names and ROI names aren't split the same way when they're compared. Patient IDs without an underscore ( MA0001_Scan.nii.gz / MA0001_ROI.mrk.json ) match fine; an underscore inside the ID itself breaks the pairing and that patient gets skipped, without stopping the rest of the batch (a warning is written to the log).

page: AutoCrop3D — crop a series of volumes
title: The interface rejects formats the crop itself accepts
text: The interface's input check only recognizes compressed volumes ( .nii.gz , .nrrd.gz , .gipl.gz ). A folder of uncompressed .nii or .nrrd files gets rejected ("Wrong type of patient file detected") even though the crop itself handles them fine: decompress them, or don't mix the two in the same batch.

page: AutoCrop3D — crop a series of volumes
title: "Use module Crop Volume for tilted images": read first
text: This is the only way to handle a genuinely rotated ROI, but it changes two things. First, it resamples the volume into the ROI's own frame: voxel values get modified, so the "no resampling, registration matrix still valid" benefit no longer applies. Second, it clears the entire Slicer scene for every patient it processes: don't use it if you have data loaded that you want to keep.

page: AutoCrop3D — crop a series of volumes
title: Generating a VTK mesh from a segmentation
text: Triggers automatically whenever "seg" appears anywhere in the output path (a Segmentations/ folder, for instance). Treat it as a secondary, fragile feature: the mesh isn't guaranteed to line up exactly with the cropped volume, every structure comes out in the same color, and a segmentation with more than six labels produces no mesh at all — with no error message.

page: AutoMatrix — apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: One matrix, one motion
text: Applied to a volume, the matrix moves its content. Applied to a landmark file, it moves the points by exactly the same motion. That's what keeps a scan and its landmarks aligned after going through AutoMatrix — as long as you use the same matrix for both.

page: AutoMatrix — apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: The mirror isn't centered on your patient
text: The reflection happens across the sagittal plane of the scene's origin, not the patient's own sagittal plane. If your patient isn't already centered in the scene, the result will come out both mirrored and shifted — plan on a registration step afterward to correct the offset.

page: AutoMatrix — apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: Some advertised formats no longer work
text: The interface still offers meshes ( .vtk , .vtp , .stl , .off , .obj ) as input scans for intraoral surfaces, and matrices as .npy — both get counted in the progress bar, but neither produces any output: each file of that kind is simply skipped, with a line in the error log. A .txt matrix only works if it's an actual ITK transform file, not a plain 4×4 array.

page: AutoMatrix — apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: A failed match gives no warning
text: If a scan's name and a matrix's name don't reduce to the same patient identifier (see above), that file is simply never transformed — no error message, no visible warning. If a patient is missing from the output, the first thing to check is that patient's file names.

page: AutoMatrix — apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: One output can overwrite another
text: If you uncheck the option that appends the matrix name to the output file, and a patient has more than one matrix, every result gets the same file name: each one overwrites the last, and only the final matrix processed survives. Keep this option checked whenever you're applying more than one matrix per patient.

page: AutoMatrix — apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: A landmark file can vanish silently
text: Some transformations (dense deformation fields, B-splines) can't be inverted mathematically. When that happens, the matching landmark file is skipped with just a warning in the log, while the volume itself still gets transformed — so a scan and its landmarks can end up out of sync with nothing on screen to flag it.

page: AutoMatrix — apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: Matrices aren't chained
text: When a patient has several matrices, each one is applied separately to the original input file: you get one output file per matrix, never a composition of one after the other.

page: BatchDentalSeg — segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: One extension to install first
text: BatchDentalSeg relies on the external Slicer extension NNUnet to run the computation. It doesn't install itself: get it through the Extensions Manager, then restart Slicer. Without it, the module shows a message and refuses to start.

page: BatchDentalSeg — segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: NasoMaxillaDentSeg: don't trust the displayed names or colors
text: On this model, the label and color shown on screen for four of the six segments don't match the real structure — for instance, what's displayed as "Upper Teeth" is actually the maxilla. This isn't just a display glitch: the value written into the exported file follows the wrong name too, and the mandibular canal segment can be dropped entirely from the export when no match is found. If you use this model, check each segment individually before trusting its name.

page: BatchDentalSeg — segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: UniversalLabDentalsegmentator does not segment the skull
text: Its description in the interface — and the upstream model's own documentation — suggests it includes the skull. It doesn't: its 55 structures are teeth, mandible, maxilla, and the mandibular canal, with no "skull" structure at all. Don't reach for this model expecting a cranial segmentation.

page: BatchDentalSeg — segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: Switching models later can wipe the others' weights
text: Re-downloading or updating DentalSegmentator's weights clears the entire models folder, including anything already downloaded for PediatricDentalsegmentator, NasoMaxillaDentSeg, and UniversalLabDentalsegmentator. If you switch between models, expect to re-download them.

page: BatchDentalSeg — segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: Your files aren't being picked up
text: Only .nii , .nii.gz , .gipl , and .gipl.gz are recognized, and only at the top level of the chosen folder — a scan in NRRD or sitting in a subfolder is silently ignored. Two different folders containing a scan with the same base name will overwrite the same output: give your files unique names.

page: CLIC — find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: The progress bar doesn't move — that's expected
text: While the tool runs, the progress bar stays at zero and nothing shows up in the Slicer scene, even after processing has finished. This is not a crash: the result file is written to disk in the output folder regardless. You have to go find it and load it yourself — see below where it lands.

page: CLIC — find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Accepted formats that don't actually work
text: The file picker also lists .nrrd , .mha , and .mhd . Don't use them: processing can only read .nii / .nii.gz , and fails on the other formats regardless of what the picker allowed.

page: CLIC — find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Linux only
text: The module has no working path on Windows, whatever the README says. Run it on a Linux Slicer installation.

page: CLIC — find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Cancel does nothing
text: It stops neither the running computation nor the underlying process. If you genuinely need to stop, close Slicer.

page: CLIC — find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: The first run needs internet access
text: Building the network downloads generic pretrained weights before the trained model is applied on top. Without a connection on the first attempt, processing fails.

page: CLIC — find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Two model files in the folder
text: With more than one model file in the models folder, whichever name sorts first alphabetically gets used, with no warning. Keep a single .pth file in that folder to avoid any ambiguity.

page: CNE — extract information from clinical notes
title: Nothing leaves your machine
text: The model runs inside Slicer's own Python, on your computer. Notes aren't sent to any online service during extraction — the only step that touches the network is the one-time model download.

page: CNE — extract information from clinical notes
title: The Ortho model won't download
text: The file the module asks for the Ortho model doesn't exist at the address listed on Hugging Face: the download fails with "Download failed or was cancelled", with no further explanation. TMJ mode downloads fine. If you pick Ortho today, expect this failure — it isn't something on your end.

page: CNE — extract information from clinical notes
title: Notes sorted into per-patient subfolders
text: CNE only looks at files sitting directly in the folder you chose, not at anything inside subfolders. A folder organized with one subfolder per patient will produce no output at all, with no error message.

page: CNE — extract information from clinical notes
title: Scanned PDF
text: PDF text extraction doesn't do OCR: if your PDF is actually a scanned image, the extracted text is empty and the note can't produce anything.

page: CNE — extract information from clinical notes
title: Tables inside a .docx
text: Only paragraph text is read from a Word document; table content is skipped. If your key information sits in a table, it never reaches the model.

page: CNE — extract information from clinical notes
title: Note too long
text: There's no chunking: a note longer than the model can read in one pass fails entirely instead of being processed in pieces. The margin is especially tight in Ortho mode.

page: CNE — extract information from clinical notes
title: No anonymization
text: Notes are read as-is, with no personal-data removal. If your files contain identifying information, run them through MedicalDataAnonymizer first if needed.

page: DOCShapeAXI — classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Three shape families, one window
text: The data type you pick is the only thing that decides which model runs and which categories come out: Mandibular Condyle — a severity stage out of 4 classes . Nasopharynx Airway Obstruction — three results produced one after another in a single run: presence or absence of obstruction ( 2 classes ), a severity stage ( 4 classes ), and a continuous ratio of obstruction between 0 and 100. Alveolar Bone Defect in Cleft — a severity stage out of 4 classes . For all three severity stages, the 4 classes are really quarter

page: DOCShapeAXI — classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: The map only shows part of what mattered
text: The model decides by combining two sources: the shape of a sampled point cloud and a rendering of several views of the mesh. The explainability map only describes the second one. If a decision leaned mostly on the point-cloud geometry, the map you see will look faint — with nothing to tell you that's the reason, rather than the decision genuinely having no clear focus.

page: DOCShapeAXI — classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Two runs, not necessarily the same result
text: The points sampled from the mesh are not drawn the same way twice. Two passes on the same files can therefore produce slightly different saliency maps, and in cases sitting near the boundary between two classes, a different predicted class.

page: DOCShapeAXI — classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: The output folder has to exist before you launch
text: If the folder you point to doesn't exist yet, the model download is simply skipped, and the error only surfaces later, when the model tries to load. Create the output folder yourself before starting.

page: DOCShapeAXI — classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Adding files mid-way has no effect
text: The list of meshes to process is only rebuilt if it doesn't already exist in the output folder. If you drop more meshes into the input folder without changing the output folder, they simply won't be processed.

page: DOCShapeAXI — classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Disk space
text: The downloaded model isn't cached: every new output folder re-downloads it in full. Across several batches, reuse the same output folder where you can, or clean up the old ones.

page: DOCShapeAXI — classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Re-running on the same folder
text: Prediction columns are overwritten in place on every re-run, but columns left over from a different task are never cleared out — they sit side by side in the csv.

page: FlexReg — register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Two ways to build the stable area
text: On an upper arch, the area is anchored on the palate: pick four reference teeth and FlexReg builds a butterfly-shaped patch around them, or draw its outline directly with the mouse. On a lower arch, with no palate to act as a stable plate, FlexReg instead relies on the mucogingival line — placed automatically — then thickens it into a band running along the gum.

page: FlexReg — register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: A graphics card is mandatory
text: Building the patch and running the registration only work with a compatible GPU. Without one, these steps fail outright — this isn't a performance nicety, it's a hard requirement of the module.

page: FlexReg — register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: "The registration only looks at the teeth I checked"
text: FlexReg aligns only the area you marked out — never the whole arch. If the result looks off away from that area, that's expected: the rest of the mesh simply follows the motion computed on the patch, it isn't registered independently.

page: FlexReg — register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Mucogingival landmarks can be unreliable
text: On the lower arch, some automatically placed points can be markedly less trusted than the others (the measured error jumps from roughly 1 mm to over 4 mm in those cases). FlexReg drops them by default and bridges the gap by interpolation — so a point can look "missing" even though it was detected.

page: FlexReg — register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: DICOM import
text: Start from already-exported .vtk or .stl files. The registration itself doesn't read DICOM.

page: FlexReg — register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Input file gets overwritten
text: Drawing the stable area and running crown segmentation both rewrite the input file, not a copy. Always keep a backup of your original scans before you start.

page: FlexReg — register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Steeply tilted arch: the patch can overshoot
text: The butterfly patch's outline is decided by flattening the arch into a projection. On a strongly tilted arch, that projection can pick up points that are actually far away in height, producing a patch that spills past the intended area — check the preview before committing.

page: GreedyReg — register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: Three modes, one real registration
text: Only Automatic Registration actually performs an intensity-based registration. Manual Alignment and Distant Registration only prepare a starting point, to be refined afterward.

page: GreedyReg — register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: "Save Registered Volume" does nothing in Distant mode
text: This mode does not produce a registered volume, only a starting matrix: the button always answers "No result to save!". Use "Save Transform Matrix" instead, or go straight to Automatic Registration to get a volume worth saving.

page: GreedyReg — register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: Misleading checkboxes in Distant mode
text: Checking several structures (cranial base, mandible, maxilla) does not combine them. Only one region is actually used, chosen by a fixed priority order (cranial base first, then mandible, then maxilla), regardless of which boxes you checked.

page: GreedyReg — register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: In batch, one failure stops everything, not always clearly
text: On a full folder, the first case that fails halts the entire run: no resume, no list of the remaining cases. In Distant mode, a failed landmark prediction does not always surface as an obvious error: the only visible sign can be a quiet "only 0 matched landmarks" in the log.

page: GreedyReg — register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: Temporary folders are never cleaned up
text: Whether after an automatic registration or a manual session, the module does not clear its working folders. On a long series, disk usage builds up; clean them yourself from time to time — but only after saving your results, since that is also where "Save Registered Volume" pulls its file from in Automatic mode.

page: MRI2CBCT — align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: Six tabs, not one button
text: Each tab has its own button and writes its files to its own folder; nothing in the module stops you from running them out of order or skipping one. Two tabs are genuinely optional (the left/right crop and the joint crop); the others only look optional — without them, the final registration starts with no starting point and won't converge.

page: MRI2CBCT — align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: An install prompt keeps coming back
text: Automatic dependency installation fails every time (a misspelled package name that doesn't exist). You'll see an installation error before almost every button, but the action carries on anyway regardless. If the rest of your setup is already in place, that changes nothing; but if condyle segmentation later fails without a clear message, this is the likely cause — the real dependency was never installed on its own, and you'll need to install it yourself.

page: MRI2CBCT — align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: Two paths that crash the module
text: In manual approximation, "Confirm & Save Alignment" crashes if the MRI volume was picked from the scene's drop-down list: only loading it through "Load from Folders Above" works reliably. And in resampling, processing T2 MRIs without also filling in the T1 fields crashes the step — always fill in both, even if one of the two folders stays empty.

page: MRI2CBCT — align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: The written matrix doesn't quite match the produced image
text: The transform file ( .tfm ) saved at the end of registration doesn't fully capture the internal computation: a reference point for the final rotation is lost on writing. The already-registered MRI the module gives you is reliable; but if you reload the matrix in another program to apply it yourself, expect a slight mismatch with the result produced here.

page: MRI2CBCT — align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: Files skipped without a word
text: Normalization and registration only accept .nii.gz — a .nii file is silently ignored, with no error. And during resampling, two files with the same name coming from different subfolders overwrite each other without warning. Use unique names per patient and check that every file you expect actually comes out.

page: MedX — summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: Two independent paths
text: MedX has two tabs, two buttons, and nothing chains them together automatically. Summarize reads your documents and writes one summary file per patient. Dashboard reads those summaries back and produces the figure page. Once summarization finishes, it's on you to switch tabs and launch the dashboard yourself — it doesn't start on its own.

page: MedX — summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: The model download button does nothing
text: Clicking the download button creates the expected folder but never puts a file in it: the field stays empty and a warning message appears. Get the model archive yourself from the GitHub releases page of the SlicerAutomatedDentalTools repository (the BART.zip file, under the "MedX" release), unzip it, then point the module at that folder.

page: MedX — summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: The dashboard progress bar never moves
text: Unlike the Summarize path, the Dashboard progress bar stays still for the whole run. That isn't a sign it's stuck: let it run and wait for dashboard.png to show up in the output folder.

page: MedX — summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: An empty input folder crashes the module
text: Running either path on a folder with no usable document raises an error instead of a clean message. Check that the folder you picked actually has files in it before you launch.

page: MedX — summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: Two runs, two different summaries
text: The model isn't deterministic: running the Summarize path again on the exact same documents won't reproduce the previous summary word for word. If you need to compare results over time, keep the _summary.txt files you already have rather than regenerating them.

title: This does not anonymise images
text: Despite the name, no DICOM tag is touched — not the patient's name, birth date, study identifier, or institution — and no face is removed from a CBCT or scanner volume. If images are what you need de-identified, this tool does nothing for you: you need a dedicated DICOM anonymiser, plus separate defacing if the volumes cover the face.

title: A failure can look like a success
text: If processing a document fails, for any reason, the output file comes out with the original text untouched — and the interface still reports "Complete!" No counter, no report, no visible warning marks the difference: a document that was never anonymised is indistinguishable from a clean one until you open it yourself. Reopen and read through every output file before handing it off or publishing it.

title: Dependency installation fails
text: It needs internet access to download Presidio and the language model. If installation errors out, check the connection and try again; Slicer will need restarting once it succeeds either way.

title: Two files with the same name, only one comes out
text: The output folder is written flat: the input's subfolder structure isn't reproduced, and if two subfolders each hold a file with the same name, the second one silently overwrites the first. Rename ahead of time if that's a risk.

title: A .csv comes out unreadable
text: It's the most fragile format here: columns aren't preserved as-is. For tabular data you need to keep usable, anonymise a separate text copy and rebuild the table by hand.

title: The interface looks frozen
text: That's expected: processing runs on Slicer's main thread. On a large folder, leave it running and don't close Slicer, even though nothing else responds in the meantime.

page: SurgMovPred — estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: A spreadsheet-only tool
text: SurgMovPred doesn't read any volume, surface, or Slicer landmark, and it doesn't touch your 3D scene: nothing is created or displayed there. Everything happens on disk — a folder of spreadsheets in, a folder of spreadsheets out.

page: SurgMovPred — estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: Each point is predicted on its own, not the whole segment
text: The 112 output values come from 112 independent models, one per value. Nothing guarantees that the ten points predicted for the maxilla, say, stay consistent with each other: the result isn't a rigid transform of the bone block, only a collection of pointwise displacements computed separately from one another. Don't reconstruct an overall movement from these numbers without checking them against each other first.

page: SurgMovPred — estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: Clicking Apply reinstalls a dependency every time
text: Clicking Apply always forces a reinstall of numpy, even when everything was already working. That makes the run slower, and swapping out a core numerical library inside an already-running Slicer session can unsettle other tools that depend on it. If another module starts misbehaving after you've used SurgMovPred, restart Slicer before looking any further.

page: SurgMovPred — estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: A missing column in the output isn't a crash
text: If one of the expected values is missing from the result, nothing errors out visibly: the model behind it was simply skipped because one of the columns it needed couldn't be found after the header cleanup. The warning stays in Slicer's log, not in the spreadsheet — if your output has almost no predicted columns, compare your headers against the example spreadsheet before looking elsewhere.

page: SurgMovPred — estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: Check which sheet is active in your workbook
text: Only the first sheet of an .xlsx or .ods file is read. If your per-patient measurements aren't on the first sheet, SurgMovPred will read a different one — or an empty one — without saying so.

page: SurgMovPred — estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: The test-files button doesn't fill anything in by itself
text: It does download an archive, but it only fills in the input and output folders if another module's test data (VFACE's) is already present on the machine. On a machine without it, clicking the button has no visible effect.

page: SurgMovPred — estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: All models are loaded on every run
text: SurgMovPred loads all 112 models into memory as soon as it runs, even for a single patient or a single value you actually care about — roughly 1.5 GB of RAM before it even reads your spreadsheet. Plan for that on a memory-constrained machine.

title: The heaviest module in the extension
text: VFACE is not a standalone tool: it's an orchestrator that chains, one after another, six other modules of the extension (resampling, orientation, bone segmentation, registration, dental surface segmentation, classification). On a batch of patients, expect the full run to be long — on the order of an hour per patient depending on your machine — and it keeps the other tools busy while it runs. Plan to launch it when you don't need the other modules at the same time, typically overnight on a series.

title: Resuming an interrupted batch costs almost as much as starting over
text: If you interrupt a run and rerun it for only some patients — flagged or corrected — the slowest steps of the pipeline (bone segmentation, registration, dental surface segmentation) are still replayed for every patient in the batch , not just the ones you flagged. Selective resume only saves time on the fast steps; on a large batch, don't expect to save much compared to a full rerun.

title: Upstream results are a starting point
text: The landmarks and registrations produced along the way can be imperfect. That's what the review pauses are for: use them to check and correct before the following steps build on them, since an early error propagates to every step downstream.

title: Disk space
text: Without a properly set, valid output folder, or depending on the "keep intermediate files" option, the automatic cleanup at the end of a run can behave unexpectedly. Always double-check that the output folder you point to is the right one before launching a batch, and keep an eye on available disk space on long series.

title: Coupling worth knowing
text: ALI , AREG , ASO , DOCShapeAXI and FlexReg share the same conda environment shapeaxi , on Python 3.12 . A change to the Python version breaks all of them at once. Details in FlexReg , Environment section.
